Independent finite check at N=4 compared the least singular value against 1/(N sqrt(rho(K^(-1)W/N^2))) to about 10^(-15). Replay method: form the lower bidiagonal matrix and the independent symmetric matrix with entries sqrt(w_i w_j) min(i,j)/N^2; compare the smallest singular value with the transformed top eigenvalue. For J_i=1 the closed finite answer 2 sin(pi/(4N+2)) also checks the boundary and factor of two.
correctness.rationale: The conclusion is for the least singular value (one-fermion energy at the stated Hamiltonian normalization), not a parity-constrained gap. Factoring M=(I+S)diag(h) and setting z_i=(-1)^i h_i v_i gives the pinned-left/free-right string quotient with exact mass w_N=1 and w_i=J_i^(-2) otherwise. Its stiffness is a squared first difference, whose inverse is min(i,j). Scaling gives the Green operator with atomic mass on j/N. The Lipschitz-operator bound follows by integrating against the cumulative mass discrepancy: both min(x,y)f(y) and 1_{y>x}f(y) have uniformly bounded variation in y for ||f||_Lip<=1, controlling the supremum and the a.e. derivative. The discrepancy is at most the maximum absolute centered partial sum divided by N plus O(1/N); the strong law and Kolmogorov maximal inequality give a.s. convergence and O_P(N^-1/2), respectively. The limiting map has a bounded image in C^{1,1}, so is compact in Lip. With k=pi/2 the top simple isolated eigenvalue is m/k^2, with right sine mode u and left functional 2 integral(u f); spectral separation and norm convergence identify the nearby eigenvalue with the top finite-matrix eigenvalue. The simple-eigenvalue expansion has a quadratic remainder. Its linear term is the empirical sum of centered masses with coefficient 2 sin^2(kj/N)/(k^2 N), up to O(1/N) from quadrature and the endpoint. The bounded weighted triangular-array CLT uses integral sin^4=3/8; the map rho -> rho^(-1/2) gives variance 3 pi^2 s^2/(32 m^3). For s^2=0 the centered sum vanishes and the remainder at sqrt(N) scale goes to zero. No extrapolation to heavy tails, other balance profiles or parity-constrained excitations is made.
residual_risks: The finite checks are normalization and matrix-identity checks, not evidence of convergence in law on their own. The theorem uses bounded iid masses and one shared infinite sequence.
